title: Operating SSC on real databases: provider isolation and backend constraints
summary: Semantic Source Store is backend-neutral. DatabaseBackendSelector is the sole runtime provider-package selection boundary: it resolves deployment configuration, loads only the selected provider package with Package~loadPackage(), and hands the returned common database object/executor to SemanticSourceDatabaseComposition. This is required not only for clean deployment but because NoSQLServer and Database Core publish overlapping public database class names with different semantics.
invariants: Neutral SSC source must not ::requires NoSQLServer.cls, database_core.cls, PostgreSQLNativeBackend, MySQL implementation classes, or any other concrete database provider.

Backend selection is configuration-only. OOREXX_DATABASE_PROVIDER selects the logical provider; OOREXX_DATABASE_PROVIDER_PACKAGE and OOREXX_DATABASE_PROVIDER_CLASS may override package resolution. Switching backend must not require Codex, another model, or a human to edit SSC source or rewrite ::requires directives.
Only the selected provider package is loaded into an ooRexx process. Provider public classes are resolved inside that Package and are not imported into the neutral caller package.
NoSQLServer and Database Core must not be statically loaded side by side into one caller package because names such as DatabaseRow and DatabaseResult overlap while their observable semantics differ.
The NoSQLServer provider returns the existing namespaced FileDatabaseEngine~databaseCore compatibility facade; native NoSQLServer API semantics remain unchanged.
The PostgreSQL provider may load database_core.cls and PostgreSQLNativeBackend inside its selected provider package; that dependency must not leak into SSC's package namespace.
Unknown, incomplete, or unloadable provider configuration fails closed. There is no silent fallback to a different backend after selection.
Never qualify SSC persistence with test/NoSQLServer.cls; run live persistence tests against a real selected backend.

Historical NoSQLServer v0.79 caveats remain relevant to old deployments: UPDATE evaluated some quoted literals as expressions, IN lists were absent, join keys were qualified, and CRLF source was not lossless. Those are backend-version constraints, not reasons to couple SSC to NoSQLServer.
Install Crypto's Foreign Runtime provider at the composition root where required by the selected runtime; cryptographic acceleration and database provider selection remain separate responsibilities.
Never name an ooRexx variable RESULT in code that also uses bare message instructions when the RESULT special variable would change semantics.

evidence.qualification: The generic selector/package-isolation regression is wired into the native database backend test suite. This sphere update records source-reviewed architecture; it does not claim a fresh live PostgreSQL server qualification.
evidence.prior_live_evidence: Library deployment log records ed209i job ssc-dev23-selector-pg-smoke9 completing rc=0 on 2026-10-05 with OOREXX_DATABASE_PROVIDER=POSTGRESQL, the isolated PostgreSQL provider package, SSC_DB_PORT/SSC_DB_NAME/SSC_DB_USER, and SSC_POSTGRESQL_BRIDGE. This is prior deployment evidence, not a fresh qualification of today's GitHub revision.
